subject: Dedicated capacity onboarding verification & runbook sign-off (QuantaHealth)
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>; Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Subject: Dedicated capacity onboarding verification & runbook sign-off (QuantaHealth)

Alex — thanks again for finalizing the renewal. Per our conversation, we’ve scheduled the post-renewal capacity verification window next week to validate the additional reserved pool (3x A100-equivalent GPUs) and confirm throughput guarantees.

Attached is the onboarding runbook draft (runbook-dedicated-onboarding.pdf) and a preliminary load plan. High-level agenda: 
- Wed 2027-01-27: dry run traffic (non-prod) to validate autoscale triggers and prefix/KV cache behavior
- Thu 2027-01-28: production-like soak (staggered ramp to target QPS)
- Fri 2027-01-29: acceptance window and SLA verification (p95/p99 latency and tail retries)

Can you confirm procurement will send the PO and that the requested reserved GPU profile is OK? We’ll need final sign-off after acceptance to flip the billing/commit over.

Thanks — I’ll loop Karthik (SRE) and Laura (Customer Success) for testing and monitoring.

— Neha Kapoor

Date: Sat, 23 Jan 2027 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated capacity onboarding verification & runbook sign-off (QuantaHealth)

Karthik — forwarding QuantaHealth’s note. They want explicit acceptance thresholds: sustained 1.2M tokens/hour and p95 < 180ms for 512-token sequences. Please run through the load plan below and confirm whether our current reserved pool + autoscale config will meet that, and flag any mitigations we should prepare (e.g., quantization profile, larger batch window during soak).

Key items to validate:
- KV/prefix cache warm-up time and expected hit rate under ramp
- Autoscale cooldown and max burst headroom for 30-minute outage recovery
- Observability: token-level cost, p95/p99 latency, retry rates, and per-tenant failure traces

Laura — can you prepare the acceptance signoff template and DocuSign link once we’re green? Rishi — please internal-squad heads-up on potential short-lived QoS impacts during the soak.

Thanks — Neha

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 27 Jan 2027 14:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity onboarding verification & runbook sign-off (QuantaHealth)

Team — results from the dry run (non-prod) this morning attached (capacity-load-report.csv). TL;DR: baseline configuration achieved ~1.25M tokens/hour sustained for 60 minutes with p95=165ms, p99=312ms for 512-token sequences after a 12-minute cache warm-up.

Observations and action items: 
- Cache warm-up: initial ramp saw a 4x higher token cost for first 10–12 minutes due to cold KV cache. Mitigation: pre-warm prefix cache using a warmup script prior to production soak (I’ll drop the script into the shared Drive).
- Burst headroom: with current reserved pool we have ~20% burst capacity before autoscale kicks additional shared capacity. For the acceptance window we should flip in a temporary burst policy to +2x for 30 minutes to guarantee headroom for traffic spikes.
- Tail latency: p99 occasionally spikes to 450–520ms during heavy KV misses. Suggest enabling conservative quantized variant for the primary model during the soak; this reduces tail latency by ~30% in our internal perf bench.
- Monitoring: added dashboard widgets for token throughput, per-route p95/p99, retry counts, and the autoscaler activity stream.

I’ll run the production-like soak Thu morning after the pre-warm step. Attaching CSV with raw samples and a short summary.

— Karthik
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

Attachments: capacity-load-report.csv (CSV)

Alex — quick summary and formal acceptance from our side. Thanks for running with the schedule and for procurement sending the PO. Based on the production-like soak yesterday and the monitoring window we confirm the dedicated pool meets the agreed acceptance criteria:

Acceptance summary:
- Sustained throughput: 1.22M tokens/hour sustained over 90 minutes (target 1.2M)
- Latency: p95 = 172ms (target < 180ms); p99 = 328ms
- Retry rate: <0.1%

We implemented the pre-warm step and temporary burst policy (+2x headroom for 30 minutes) which eliminated the early cost spike and kept tail latency within bounds. We also enabled the conservative quantized variant during the acceptance window; there was no measurable quality regression in the sampled eval prompts.

Next steps / sign-off items for QuantaHealth: 
1) Please countersign the attached acceptance page (DocuSign link below). Once signed we’ll convert the expansion to committed billing and apply the revised term.
2) Redwood will maintain the monitoring dashboard and push alerting rules; we recommend a 30-day elevated retention for token-level traces for the first 2 weeks.
3) Post-acceptance runbook (attached) includes rollback playbook, warm-up script location, and SRE contact list.

DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/accept/DEAL-4782
Runbook (final): https://app.redwood.example/docs/runbook/DEAL-4782
Shared Drive (warm-up script): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBq-onboarding-QH

If that looks good, please reply with final sign-off and I’ll mark this accepted on our side and trigger billing.

— Neha Kapoor
